translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month: an edict that General of Valiant Cavalry Yan Pu was to fortify Qiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter he ordered Yan Pu, General of Valiant Cavalry, to fortify Qiancheng.

sentences.zh: 十有二月丁亥，杏城羌酋狄溫子率三千餘家內附。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day dinghai: Di Wenzi, Qiang chief of Xingcheng, led more than three thousand households to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the twelfth month Di Wenzi, Qiang chief of Xingcheng, brought more than three thousand households in submission.

sentences.zh: 是歲，劉裕廢殺其主司馬德文，僭自稱皇帝，號宋。

translations.literal: That year Liu Yu deposed and killed his lord Sima Dewen, presumptuously styled himself emperor, and took the dynastic name Song.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liu Yu deposed and killed his lord Sima Dewen, seized the throne, and styled his dynasty Song.

sentences.zh: 李歆為沮渠蒙遜所滅，歆弟恂自立於敦煌。

translations.literal: Li Xin was destroyed by Juqu Mengxun; Xin's younger brother Xun established himself at Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin fell to Juqu Mengxun; his younger brother Xun set himself up at Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月辛未，行幸公陽。

translations.literal: Year 6, spring, first month, day xinwei: traveled to Gongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, on the xinwei day of the first month of spring, he went to Gongyang.

sentences.zh: 二月，調民二十戶輸戎馬一匹、大牛一頭。

translations.literal: Second month: twenty households per levy were to supply one war horse and one great ox.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he levied one war horse and one great ox for every twenty households.

sentences.zh: 三月甲子，陽平王熙薨。

translations.literal: Third month, day jiazi: Prince of Yangping Xi died.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the third month Xi, Prince of Yangping, died.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，制六部民，羊滿百口輸戎馬一匹。

translations.literal: On yihai a regulation for the six divisions: for every hundred sheep, one war horse was to be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day he ordered that among the six divisions, every hundred sheep owed one war horse.

sentences.zh: 發京師六千人築苑，起自舊苑，東包白登，周回三十餘里。

translations.literal: Six thousand men of the capital were mobilized to build a park, beginning from the old park, wrapping east around Baideng, thirty-odd li in circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand men of the capital were set to build a park from the old grounds, wrapping east around Baideng for more than thirty li.

sentences.zh: 夏六月乙酉，北巡，至蟠羊山。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month, day yiyou: toured north to Mount Panyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the sixth month of summer he toured north to Mount Panyang.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，西巡，獵于柞山，親射虎，獲之，遂至于河。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: toured west, hunted at Mount Zha, personally shot a tiger and took it, then reached the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he toured west, hunted at Mount Zha, shot a tiger himself, and came to the river.

sentences.zh: 八月庚子，大獮于犢渚。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day gengzi: great hunt at Duzhu.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the eighth month he held a great hunt at Duzhu.

sentences.zh: 九月庚戌，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day gengxu: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day of the ninth month the court returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 壬申，劉裕遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On renshen Liu Yu sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day Liu Yu sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己亥，行幸代。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jihai: traveled to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day of the tenth month of winter he went to Dai.

sentences.zh: 十有二月丙申，西巡狩，至于雲中。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day bingshen: toured west on hunt to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day of the twelfth month he hunted west to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 是歲，沮渠蒙遜滅李恂。

translations.literal: That year Juqu Mengxun destroyed Li Xun.
translations.idiomatic: That year Juqu Mengxun overthrew Li Xun.

sentences.zh: 七年春正月甲辰朔，自雲中西行，幸屋竇城，賜從者大酺三日、蕃渠帥繒帛各有差。

translations.literal: Year 7, spring, first month, day jiachen, first of month: from Yunzhong he traveled west, visited Wudou City, granted his followers a great feast for three days, and gave the tribal chiefs silk in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, on the first jiachen day of the first month of spring, he left Yunzhong and went west to Wudou City, feasted his followers for three days, and gave the tribal chiefs silk according to rank.

sentences.zh: 二月丙戌，車駕還宮，賜從者布帛各有差，大饗于西宮。

translations.literal: Second month, day bingxu: the imperial carriage returned to the palace, granted cloth and silk to his followers in differing amounts, and held a grand feast in the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day of the second month the court returned to the palace, rewarded the followers with cloth and silk according to rank, and held a grand feast in the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 三月乙丑，河南王曜薨。

translations.literal: Third month, day yichou: Prince of Henan Yao died.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the third month Yao, Prince of Henan, died.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲戌，封皇子燾為泰平王，燾，字佛釐，拜相國，加大將軍；

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day jiaxu: enfeoffed the imperial son Tao as Prince of Taiping, Tao styled Foli, appointed Chancellor of State and given the additional title Grand General;
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day of the fourth month of summer he enfeoffed his son Tao as Prince of Taiping—Tao, styled Foli—appointed him Chancellor of State, and gave him the additional rank of Grand General;

sentences.zh: 丕為樂平王，加車騎大將軍；

translations.literal: Pi as Prince of Leping, given the additional title General of Chariots and Cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: Pi as Prince of Leping, with the additional rank of General of Chariots and Cavalry;

sentences.zh: 彌為安定王，加衞大將軍；

translations.literal: Mi as Prince of Anding, given the additional title General of the Guard;
translations.idiomatic: Mi as Prince of Anding, with the additional rank of General of the Guard;

sentences.zh: 範為樂安王，加中軍大將軍；

translations.literal: Fan as Prince of Le'an, given the additional title General of the Central Army;
translations.idiomatic: Fan as Prince of Le'an, with the additional rank of General of the Central Army;

sentences.zh: 健為永昌王，加撫軍大將軍；

translations.literal: Jian as Prince of Yongchang, given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Army;
translations.idiomatic: Jian as Prince of Yongchang, with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Army;

sentences.zh: 崇為建寧王，加輔國大將軍；

translations.literal: Chong as Prince of Jianning, given the additional title General Who Assists the State;
translations.idiomatic: Chong as Prince of Jianning, with the additional rank of General Who Assists the State;

sentences.zh: 俊為新興王，加鎮軍大將軍；

translations.literal: Jun as Prince of Xinxing, given the additional title General Who Garrisons the Army;
translations.idiomatic: Jun as Prince of Xinxing, with the additional rank of General Who Garrisons the Army;

sentences.zh: 獻懷長公主子嵇敬，封長樂王，拜大司馬、大將軍。

translations.literal: Ji Jing, son of the Princess of Xianhuai, was enfeoffed as Prince of Changle and appointed Grand Marshal and Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: and Ji Jing, son of the Princess of Xianhuai, was made Prince of Changle and appointed Grand Marshal and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 初，帝素服寒食散，頻年動發，不堪萬機，五月，詔皇太子臨朝聽政。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had long taken the Cold-Food Powder in plain dress; year after year fits recurred, and he could not bear the myriad affairs; in the fifth month an edict that the Crown Prince was to preside at court and hear government.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, the Emperor had taken the Cold-Food Powder and worn plain dress; fits returned year after year until he could no longer bear the weight of rule. In the fifth month he ordered the Crown Prince to preside at court and hear government.

sentences.zh: 是月，泰平王攝政。

translations.literal: That month the Prince of Taiping held regency.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Prince of Taiping held the regency.

sentences.zh: 劉裕卒，子義符僭立。

translations.literal: Liu Yu died; his son Yifu presumptuously succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu died; his son Yifu seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，詔假司空奚斤節，都督前鋒諸軍事，為晉兵大將軍、行揚州刺史，交阯侯周幾為宋兵將軍、交州刺史，安固子公孫表為吳兵將軍、廣州刺史，前鋒伐劉義符。

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month: an edict granting Acting Minister of Works Xi Jin credentials, making him Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard Armies, Grand General of Jin Troops and Acting Governor of Yangzhou; Marquis of Jiaozhi Zhou Ji as General of Song Troops and Governor of Jiao; Anguozi Gongsun Biao as General of Wu Troops and Governor of Guang—the vanguard to campaign against Liu Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn he granted Xi Jin, Acting Minister of Works, credentials as Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard, Grand General of Jin Troops and acting governor of Yangzhou; Zhou Ji, Marquis of Jiaozhi, as General of Song Troops and governor of Jiao; and Gongsun Biao, Anguozi, as General of Wu Troops and governor of Guang—to lead the vanguard against Liu Yifu.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，幸灅南宮，遂如廣寧。

translations.literal: On yisi he visited Juan South Palace and then went to Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day he went to Juan South Palace and then on to Guangning.

sentences.zh: 己酉，詔泰平王率百國以法駕田于東苑，車乘服物皆以乘輿之副。

translations.literal: On jiyou an edict that the Prince of Taiping was to lead the hundred states in hunting by imperial rites in the Eastern Park; chariots, mounts, and regalia were all to use the spare set of the imperial equipage.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day he ordered the Prince of Taiping to lead the hundred states in a hunt by imperial rite in the Eastern Park, with chariots, mounts, and regalia all drawn from the imperial spare equipage.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，築平城外郭，周回三十二里。

translations.literal: On xinhai the outer wall of Pingcheng was built, thirty-two li in circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day the outer wall of Pingcheng was built, thirty-two li around.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，幸橋山，遣使者祠黃帝、唐堯廟。

translations.literal: On xinyou he visited Bridge Mountain and sent envoys to sacrifice at the temples of the Yellow Emperor and Tang Yao.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day he went to Bridge Mountain and sent envoys with the great sacrifice to the temples of the Yellow Emperor and Tang Yao.

sentences.zh: 因東幸幽州，見耆年，問其所苦，賜爵號。

translations.literal: Then east he visited Youzhou, saw the aged, asked what troubled them, and granted noble titles.
translations.idiomatic: Then he toured east to Youzhou, received the aged, asked their hardships, and granted noble titles.

sentences.zh: 分遣使者循行州郡，觀察風俗。

translations.literal: He separately dispatched envoys to tour the provinces and observe local custom.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to tour the provinces and observe local custom.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲戌，車駕還宮，復所過田租之半。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jiaxu: the imperial carriage returned to the palace and remitted half the field rent everywhere he had passed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the jiaxu day, the court returned to the palace and remitted half the field rent along the route.

sentences.zh: 奚斤伐滑臺不克，帝怒，議親南討，為其聲援。

translations.literal: Xi Jin attacked Huatai but did not prevail; the Emperor was angry and debated a personal southern campaign to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin besieged Huatai without success; the Emperor was angry and considered marching south himself to support the attack.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，車駕南巡，出自天門關，踰恒嶺。

translations.literal: On renchen the imperial carriage toured south, leaving by Tianmen Pass and crossing Mount Heng.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day the court turned south, left by Tianmen Pass, and crossed Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 四方蕃附大人各率所部從者五萬餘人。

translations.literal: Attached great men of the four directions each led their divisions; followers numbered more than fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Great men of the submitted peoples from the four directions each led their bands, more than fifty thousand followers in all.

sentences.zh: 十有一月，泰平王親統六軍出鎮塞上，安定王彌與北新公安同居守。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: the Prince of Taiping personally commanded the six armies and went out to garrison the frontier; the Prince of Anding Mi and the Duke of Beixin An Tong remained to guard together.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Prince of Taiping took personal command of the six armies and marched to hold the border; the Prince of Anding Mi and An Tong, Duke of Beixin, stayed behind to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 丙午，曲赦司州殊死已下。

translations.literal: On bingwu a partial amnesty was granted in Bing province for offenses below capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day he granted a partial amnesty in Bing province for all crimes short of capital offense.

sentences.zh: 劉義符東郡太守王景度棄滑臺走。

translations.literal: Liu Yifu's Administrator of Dongjun Wang Jingdu abandoned Huatai and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingdu, Administrator of Dongjun under Liu Yifu, abandoned Huatai and fled.

sentences.zh: 詔成皐侯元苟兒為兗州刺史，鎮滑臺。

translations.literal: An edict that Marquis of Chenggao Yuan Gou'er was Governor of Yanzhou and was to garrison Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yuan Gou'er, Marquis of Chenggao, governor of Yanzhou to garrison Huatai.

sentences.zh: 十有二月，遣壽光侯叔孫建等率眾自平原東渡，徇下青、兗諸郡。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Marquis of Shouguang Shusun Jian and others led their masses east from Pingyuan across the river and subdued the commanderies of Qing and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Shusun Jian, Marquis of Shouguang, and others led their forces east from Pingyuan across the river and overran the commanderies of Qing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 劉義符兗州刺史徐琰聞渡河，棄守走，叔孫建遂東入青州。

translations.literal: Liu Yifu's Governor of Yanzhou Xu Yan heard they had crossed the river, abandoned his post and fled; Shusun Jian then entered Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Yan, governor of Yanzhou under Liu Yifu, heard they had crossed the river, he abandoned his post and fled; Shusun Jian then entered Qing province.

sentences.zh: 司馬愛之、秀之先聚黨濟東，皆率眾來降。

translations.literal: Sima Aizhi and Xiuzhi had earlier gathered bands east of the Ji; both led their masses to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Aizhi and Sima Xiuzhi had earlier raised bands east of the Ji; both now brought their followers in surrender.

sentences.zh: 八年正月丙辰，行幸鄴，存恤民俗。

translations.literal: Year 8, spring, first month, day bingchen: traveled to Ye and comforted the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, on the bingchen day of the first month of spring, he went to Ye and comforted the people.

sentences.zh: 司空奚斤既平兗豫，還圍虎牢，劉義符守將毛德祖距守不下。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xi Jin had already pacified Yan and Yu and returned to besiege Hulao; Liu Yifu's defending general Mao Dezu held firm and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin, Minister of Works, had pacified Yan and Yu and returned to besiege Hulao, but Mao Dezu, Liu Yifu's garrison commander, held firm and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 河東蜀薛定、薛輔率五千餘家內屬。

translations.literal: The Shu of Hedong, Xue Ding and Xue Fu, led more than five thousand households to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ding and Xue Fu of the Shu of Hedong brought more than five thousand households in submission.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕犯塞。

translations.literal: The Rouran raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran struck the border.

sentences.zh: 二月戊辰，築長城於長川之南，起自赤城，西至五原，延袤二千餘里，備置戍衞。

translations.literal: Second month, day wuchen: the Long Wall was built south of the Changchuan, beginning at Chicheng and reaching west to Wuyuan, more than two thousand li in extent, with garrisons set along it.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the second month the Long Wall was built south of the Changchuan from Chicheng west to Wuyuan, more than two thousand li long, with garrisons posted along its length.

sentences.zh: 三月乙巳，帝田於鄴南韓陵山，幸汲郡，至于枋頭。

translations.literal: Third month, day yisi: the Emperor hunted south of Ye at Mount Hanling, visited Ji commandery, and reached Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the third month he hunted south of Ye at Mount Hanling, visited Ji commandery, and came to Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，濟自靈昌津，幸陳留、東郡。

translations.literal: On yimao he crossed from Lingchang Ford and visited Chenliu and Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day he crossed at Lingchang Ford and visited Chenliu and Dongjun.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，濟河而北，西之河內，造浮橋於冶坂津。

translations.literal: On yichou he crossed the river north, went west to Henei, and built a pontoon bridge at Yebai Ford.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day he crossed north of the river, went west to Henei, and built a pontoon bridge at Yebai Ford.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，幸三會屋侯泉，詔皇太子率百官以從。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: visited Sanhui Wuhou Spring; an edict that the Crown Prince was to lead the hundred officials in following.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he went to Sanhui Wuhou Spring and ordered the Crown Prince to lead the hundred officials in attendance.

sentences.zh: 八月，幸馬邑，觀于灅源。

translations.literal: Eighth month: visited Mayi and viewed the Juan source.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he went to Mayi and viewed the Juan source.

sentences.zh: 九月乙亥，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day yihai: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day of the ninth month the court returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 詔司空奚斤還京師，昌平侯娥清、交阯侯周幾等鎮枋頭。

translations.literal: An edict that Minister of Works Xi Jin was to return to the capital; Marquis of Changping E Qing and Marquis of Jiaozhi Zhou Ji were to garrison Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Xi Jin, Minister of Works, to the capital and left E Qing, Marquis of Changping, and Zhou Ji, Marquis of Jiaozhi, to garrison Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 劉義符潁川太守李元德竊入許昌，詔周幾擊之，元德遁走。

translations.literal: Liu Yifu's Administrator of Yingchuan Li Yuande stole into Xuchang; an edict that Zhou Ji was to attack him; Yuande fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuande, Administrator of Yingchuan under Liu Yifu, stole into Xuchang; Zhou Ji was ordered to attack him and Yuande fled.

sentences.zh: 幾平許昌，還軍枋頭。

translations.literal: Ji pacified Xuchang and returned the army to Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji took Xuchang and returned to Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸卯，廣西宮，起外垣牆，周回二十里。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day guimao: the Western Palace was enlarged; the outer wall was raised, twenty li in circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day of the tenth month of winter the Western Palace was enlarged and its outer wall extended twenty li around.

sentences.zh: [12]十有一月己巳，帝崩於西宮，時年三十二。

translations.literal: [12] Eleventh month, day jisi: the Emperor died in the Western Palace, aged thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: [12] On the jisi day of the eleventh month the Emperor died in the Western Palace. He was thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 遺詔以司空奚斤所獲軍實賜大臣，自司徒長孫嵩已下至士卒各有差。

translations.literal: His testamentary edict granted the military stores taken by Minister of Works Xi Jin to the great ministers; from Minister of Works Changsun Song down to the common soldiers, each received a differing share.
translations.idiomatic: His final edict distributed the booty taken by Xi Jin, Minister of Works, among the great ministers; from Changsun Song, Minister of Works, down to the common soldiers, each received a share according to rank.

sentences.zh: 十有二月庚子，上諡曰明元皇帝，葬于雲中金陵，廟稱太宗。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day gengzi: the posthumous title Emperor Mingyuan was granted; he was buried at Jinling in Yunzhong; the temple name was Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the twelfth month he was given the posthumous title Emperor Mingyuan, buried at Jinling in Yunzhong, and his temple name was Taizong.

sentences.zh: 帝禮愛儒生，好覽史傳，以劉向所撰新序、說苑於經典正義多有所闕，乃撰新集三十篇，採諸經史，該洽古義，兼資文武焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor treated Confucian scholars with ritual affection, loved to read histories, considered that Liu Xiang's New Prefaces and Garden of Stories in canonical rectitude had many lacunae, and therefore compiled a New Collection in thirty chapters, drawing on the classics and histories, covering ancient meanings comprehensively, and embracing both civil and martial learning.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor honored Confucian scholars, loved histories, and finding Liu Xiang's New Prefaces and Garden of Stories often deficient where canonical meaning was concerned, compiled a New Collection in thirty chapters drawn from the classics and histories, comprehensive in ancient learning and embracing both civil and martial themes.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：太祖英雄，北驅朔漠，末年內多釁隙。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Taizu was heroic; he drove the northern deserts before him; in his later years within the realm many fissures opened.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Taizu was a hero who drove the northern wastes before him; in his last years the realm was riven within.

sentences.zh: 明元抱純孝之心，逢梟鏡之禍，權以濟事，危而獲安，隆基固本，內和外輯。

translations.literal: Mingyuan embraced a heart of pure filial piety, met the calamity of the owl mirror, used expedience to accomplish affairs, gained safety amid peril, raised the imperial foundation and strengthened the root, and within and without were harmoniously joined.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan held pure filial devotion, met the calamity of parricide, used expedience to carry affairs through, found safety in peril, strengthened the throne and its foundations, and brought inner and outer into harmony.

sentences.zh: 以德見宗，良無愧也。

translations.literal: To be honored for virtue—truly he had no cause for shame.
translations.idiomatic: Honored for his virtue, he had nothing to be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷三 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」，卷末舊有宋人校語

translations.literal: Various editions of the table of contents for Wei Shu juan 3 mark this chapter "lacuna"; at the end of the chapter there was an old Song-dynasty collation note
translations.idiomatic: Various editions of the table of contents for Wei Shu juan 3 mark this chapter as lacunary; at the end of the chapter there was an old Song-dynasty collation note

sentences.zh: 〈殿本刪節入考證〉

translations.literal: 〈Palace edition abridgment moved into textual notes〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Palace edition abridgment moved into textual notes〉

sentences.zh: 云：「魏收書太宗紀亡，史館舊本帝紀第三卷上有白簽云：『此卷是魏澹史。

translations.literal: saying: "The Annals of Taizong in Wei Shou's Book of Wei is lost; on the old History Office copy of Basic Annals juan 3 there was a white slip reading: 'This juan is Wei Dan's history.
translations.idiomatic: saying, "Wei Shou's Annals of Taizong is lost; on the old History Office copy of Basic Annals juan 3 there was a white slip reading, 'This juan is Wei Dan's history.

sentences.zh: 』案隋書魏澹傳，澹之義例多與魏收不同，其一曰諱皇帝名，書太子字；

translations.literal: ' According to the biography of Wei Dan in the Book of Sui, Dan's principles differed in many points from Wei Shou's; one reads: taboo the emperor's name and write the crown prince's style name;
translations.idiomatic: ' According to the biography of Wei Dan in the Book of Sui, Dan's principles differed in many points from Wei Shou's; one reads: taboo the emperor's name and write the crown prince's style name;

sentences.zh: 四曰諸國君皆書曰卒。

translations.literal: fourth: for all feudal lords write that they 'died.'
translations.idiomatic: fourth: for all feudal rulers write that they 'died.'

sentences.zh: 今此卷書封皇子燾為泰平王，燾字佛釐；

translations.literal: Now this juan records enfeoffing the imperial son Tao as Prince of Taiping, Tao styled Foli;
translations.idiomatic: Now this juan records enfeoffing the imperial son Tao as Prince of Taiping, Tao styled Foli;

sentences.zh: 姚興、李暠、司馬德宗、劉裕皆書卒。

translations.literal: Yao Xing, Li Gao, Sima Dezong, and Liu Yu are all written as having 'died.'
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing, Li Gao, Sima Dezong, and Liu Yu are all written as having 'died.'

sentences.zh: 故疑為澹史。

translations.literal: Therefore it is suspected to be Dan's history.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is suspected to be Dan's history.

sentences.zh: 又案北史、高氏小史、修文殿御覽皇王部皆抄略魏收書，其間事及日有此紀所不載者；

translations.literal: Again, the Northern History, Gao clan Minor History, and Imperial Readings of the Xiūwén Hall, Royal Lineage section all excerpt Wei Shou's book in brief; among their events and dates there are matters this annals does not record;
translations.idiomatic: Again, the Northern History, Gao clan Minor History, and Imperial Readings of the Xiūwén Hall, Royal Lineage section all excerpt Wei Shou in brief; among their events and dates are matters this annals does not record;

sentences.zh: 北史本紀逐卷後論，全用魏收史臣語而微加增損，惟論明元，即與此紀史臣語全不同。

translations.literal: the Northern History basic annals after each juan has a discussion wholly using Wei Shou's historiographer language with slight additions and deletions, but the discussion of Mingyuan is entirely different from this annals' historiographer language.
translations.idiomatic: the Northern History places a discussion after each basic annals juan, wholly using Wei Shou's historiographer language with slight changes, but the discussion of Mingyuan is entirely unlike this annals' historiographer passage.

sentences.zh: 故知非魏收史明矣。

translations.literal: Therefore it is known for certain that it is not Wei Shou's history.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is known for certain that this is not Wei Shou's original text.

sentences.zh: 崇文總目有魏澹書一卷，今亦亡矣。

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Catalogue lists Wei Dan's book in one juan; it too is now lost.
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Catalogue lists Wei Dan's book in one juan; it too is now lost.

sentences.zh: 豈此篇乎？

translations.literal: Could this be that piece?
translations.idiomatic: Could this be that piece?

sentences.zh: 『泰常七年四月，封皇子燾為泰平王；

translations.literal: 'In Taichang year 7, fourth month, enfeoffed the imperial son Tao as Prince of Taiping;
translations.idiomatic: 'In Taichang year 7, fourth month, enfeoffed the imperial son Tao as Prince of Taiping;

sentences.zh: 五月，詔皇太子臨朝聽政，是月泰平王攝政』，重複不成文。

translations.literal: fifth month, edict that the crown prince preside at court and hear government; that month the Prince of Taiping held regency'—repetition that does not form coherent text.
translations.idiomatic: fifth month, edict that the crown prince preside at court and hear government; that month the Prince of Taiping held regency'—repetition that does not form coherent text.

sentences.zh: 其年九月、十月再書泰平王，明年五月、七月再書皇太子，前後乖戾。

translations.literal: That year the ninth and tenth months again record the Prince of Taiping; the next year the fifth and seventh months again record the crown prince—contradictions before and after.
translations.idiomatic: That year the ninth and tenth months again record the Prince of Taiping; the next year the fifth and seventh months again record the crown prince—contradictions before and after.

sentences.zh: 今據此紀，無立泰平王為皇太子事。

translations.literal: According to this annals, there is no matter of establishing the Prince of Taiping as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: According to this annals, there is no establishing the Prince of Taiping as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 世祖紀云：四月封泰平王，五月為監國，亦不言曾立為皇太子。

translations.literal: The Annals of Shizu says: fourth month enfeoffed the Prince of Taiping, fifth month made him overseer of the state—also without saying he was ever established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Shizu says: fourth month enfeoffed the Prince of Taiping, fifth month made him overseer of the state—also without saying he was ever established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 此紀初詔聽政，便云皇太子，後更稱泰平王。

translations.literal: This annals at first edicts hearing government and at once says crown prince; later it again calls him Prince of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: This annals at first edicts hearing government and at once says crown prince; later it again calls him Prince of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 惟北史泰常七年五月立泰平王燾為皇太子，臨朝聽政。

translations.literal: Only the Northern History, Taichang year 7 fifth month, establishes the Prince of Taiping Tao as crown prince to preside at court and hear government.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Northern History, Taichang year 7 fifth month, establishes Tao, Prince of Taiping, as crown prince to preside at court and hear government.

sentences.zh: 小史、御覽亦無立皇太子事，而自臨朝聽政後，悉稱皇太子。

translations.literal: The Minor History and Imperial Readings also have no establishing crown prince matter, but after presiding at court and hearing government they all call him crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Minor History and Imperial Readings also have no establishing crown prince, but after presiding at court and hearing government they all call him crown prince.

sentences.zh: 彼蓋出魏收史，故與此不同。

translations.literal: Those probably derive from Wei Shou's history; therefore they differ from this.
translations.idiomatic: Those probably derive from Wei Shou's history; therefore they differ from this.

sentences.zh: 隋書稱魏澹書甚簡要，不應如此重複乖戾。

translations.literal: The Book of Sui says Wei Dan's book was very concise; it should not be so repetitious and contradictory.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Sui says Wei Dan's book was very concise; it should not be so repetitious and contradictory.

sentences.zh: 疑此卷雖存，亦殘缺脫誤。

translations.literal: It is suspected that though this juan survives, it is also defective, lacunary, and erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: It is suspected that though this juan survives, it is also defective, lacunary, and erroneous.

sentences.zh: 」今按宋人考證此紀非魏收書原文，並認為可能是殘存的魏澹魏書。

translations.literal: " Now according to the Song-dynasty textual note, this annals is not Wei Shou's original text and is thought to be a surviving portion of Wei Dan's Book of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " Now according to the Song-dynasty textual note, this annals is not Wei Shou's original text and is thought to be a surviving portion of Wei Dan's Book of Wei.

sentences.zh: 今以沿自修文殿御覽的太平御覽卷一０二和北史卷一魏紀中明元紀與此卷對校，也可證宋人判斷是對的。

translations.literal: Collating this juan against the Taiping Imperial Readings juan 102, derived from the Imperial Readings of the Xiūwén Hall, and the Northern History juan 1 Wei Annals, Annals of Mingyuan, also confirms the Song judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Collating this juan against Taiping Imperial Readings juan 102, derived from the Imperial Readings of the Xiūwén Hall, and Northern History juan 1, Wei Annals, Annals of Mingyuan, also confirms the Song judgment.

sentences.zh: 宋初魏收書此紀已缺，故景德二年

translations.literal: In early Song Wei Shou's book already lacked this annals; therefore in Jingde year 2
translations.idiomatic: In early Song Wei Shou's book already lacked this annals; therefore in Jingde year 2

sentences.zh: 編冊府元龜時有關諸條，都和今補本此紀相同。

translations.literal: when compiling the Prime Tortoise, related entries all match this supplemented annals.
translations.idiomatic: when compiling the Prime Tortoise, related entries all match this supplemented annals.

sentences.zh: 但也有個別字句不見今補本，不知是刻本脫文，還是校刊時

translations.literal: But there are also individual words and phrases not seen in the present supplemented text; it is unknown whether they are omissions of the printed edition or of the edition used at collation
translations.idiomatic: But there are also individual words and phrases not seen in the present supplemented text; it is unknown whether they are omissions of the printed edition or of the edition used at collation

sentences.zh: 〈嘉祐六年

translations.literal: 〈Jiayou year 6
translations.idiomatic: 〈Jiayou year 6

sentences.zh: (一０六一)
後〉

translations.literal: later〉
translations.idiomatic: later〉

sentences.zh: 所據本又有殘缺。

translations.literal: the base text also had lacunae.
translations.idiomatic: the base text also had lacunae.

sentences.zh: 壬申即皇帝位 北史卷一魏紀一「壬申」作「壬午」。

translations.literal: On renshen he ascended the imperial throne: Northern History juan 1 Wei Annals 1 reads "renwu" for "renshen."
translations.idiomatic: On renshen he ascended the imperial throne: Northern History juan 1, Wei Annals 1, reads "renwu" for "renshen."

sentences.zh: 按是年十月丙辰朔，壬申是十七日，壬午是二十七日。

translations.literal: According to this, that year the tenth month had first day bingchen; renshen was the seventeenth day, renwu the twenty-seventh.
translations.idiomatic: That year the tenth month had first day bingchen; renshen was the seventeenth day, renwu the twenty-seventh.

sentences.zh: 拓跋珪被殺在本月戊辰即十三日，拓跋嗣先已逃避在外，據卷一六清河王紹傳、卷三四王洛兒傳，自拓跋嗣聞變還來到繼位，中間有一段事情，決非二三天能辦，疑作「壬午」是。
